title: WAVES: Benchmarking the Robustness of Image Watermarks
limitations: The normalization and attack grids are benchmark-specific. No F5 result, theorem of encoder independence, or calibrated SDXL operating point is supplied.

title: Robust Watermarking Using Generative Priors Against Image Editing: From Benchmarking to Advances
limitations: This is an author evaluation, not a native universal cutoff. Training on editing proxies and paper/release lineage mismatch limit the inference of unseen encoder transfer.

title: UnMarker: A Universal Attack on Defensive Image Watermarking
limitations: Broad universal-removal language exceeds what a finite method/grid evaluation can prove. Selected losses and image sets are still conditional choices. No exact attack was run against F5 here.

title: MarkNull : Model-Agnostic Watermark Removal in AI-Generated Images via On-Manifold Latent Manipulation
limitations: This is an adaptive trained attacker with method/dataset choices, not the frozen honest SDXL regenerator. Cross-method averages can mix different clean hosts and endpoint classes.

title: RAVEN : Erasing Invisible Watermarks via Novel View Synthesis
limitations: Novel-view editing changes geometry and is outside the frozen T3 empty-prompt regeneration grid. Prompt/scene consistency is not proof of image identity or imperceptibility.

title: Watermarks Attack Watermarks: Re-Watermarking as a Generic Removal Strategy
limitations: These attack and side-information conditions do not match the fixed core. Its normalized quality is not our PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS caliper set or an imagewise causal match.

title: Invisible Image Watermarks Are Provably Removable Using Generative AI
limitations: A real VAE posterior has input-dependent mean and variance. Posterior sampling, mode-only D1, changed prompts and preprocessing are not automatically the same theorem. Large encoder gain weakens an impossibility bound; it does not prove survival.

title: An undetectable watermark for generative image models
limitations: Public deterministic F5 chips, content-derived codes and expected-message checks do not inherit PRC secrecy, undetectability, unforgeability or random-key quantifiers.

title: Image Watermarks are Removable Using Controllable Regeneration from Clean Noise
limitations: This is not pixel diffusion or a ready independently trained replacement for the current SDXL path. Its strong conditional control and trained/adaptive attack are outside core.

title: Watermark Anything with Localized Messages
limitations: Neither the paper calibration nor the random-message tail establishes image FPR for the released MIT model. The official semihard raw-logit threshold differs from a tempting sigmoid-mean implementation.

title: SDXL: Improving Latent Diffusion Models for High-Resolution Image Synthesis
limitations: The paper establishes a different autoencoder training run, not independence of training data, learned features, latent directions or generative priors. The core excludes the refiner, so its behavior cannot inherit complete base-plus-refiner preference claims.

title: DREW: Towards Robust Data Provenance by Leveraging Error-Controlled Watermarking
limitations: Retrieval success is not authenticity, exclusive ownership or secure content binding. This paper is direct prior art for a registry hybrid, so an unqualified first-hybrid claim is untenable; it does not authorize adding a registry here.

title: BrushOff: Stroke-Based Re-rendering as a Watermark Removal Attack on Paintings
limitations: Painting-only domain, one renderer, fixed payload, changed probes after results and visible texture changes limit generality. VINE-only quality does not prove cross-arm distortion equivalence. No F5 output was attacked.

title: Watermarks and Fingerprints as Soft Bindings for Content Provenance: An Open-Licence Benchmark for Images, Audio and Video
limitations: Open paper/code licenses do not automatically grant all model/media uses. Its calibration split and combined score do not authorize held-out access, post-hoc cutoffs or a new score in this study.
